A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 50-page SAFE-NET study. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main text and Appendices A–E, including figures, tables and equations, without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original PDE-solving experiments, runtime measurements and spectral analyses in Section 5, with additional experiments and ablations in Appendices A and C.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices A and C, including PDE accuracy comparisons and architectural ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.1 retain the same adaptive Fourier features, domain-knowledge features, normalization and single-hidden-layer architecture. Training and optimization procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight PDE tasks described in Table 2 and Appendix B, plus the non-homogeneous-boundary heat scenario in Appendix C.3. No evaluated coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain PINN, FLS-PINN, W-PINN, RBA-PINN, RFF, RBF and RBF-P as comparators. Appendix D's separately attributed literature results are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendices A–C retain identical sampling, preprocessing, relative L2 error evaluation, model configurations, 40,000-iteration hybrid optimizer schedules and 100,000-iteration Adam-only settings.

E4.justification: The optimizer analyses and ablations of activation functions, feature counts, initialization, depth, normalization and domain-knowledge features are unchanged. The boundary-condition test and Hessian spectral analyses are also retained identically.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five random initializations/seeds and identical statistical reporting practices. Appendix C.4 also retains the same stochastic spectral-estimation procedure and sample count.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and rankings match throughout both PDFs. For example, SAFE-NET's wave error remains 1.21e-3 in Table 3, and its non-homogeneous heat error remains 2.11e-4 in Table 20.

T1.justification: The Fourier derivations in Section 3.1, NTK definition and idealized conditioning argument in Section 6, and appendix equations are identical. No mathematical assumptions, definitions or reasoning are revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and Section 7 retain the same contributions and claims about feature engineering, conditioning, accuracy and computational efficiency. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Explanations of conditioning and optimizer stability remain unchanged, as do qualifications concerning shocks, discontinuities and high-dimensional scaling. Appendices D–E retain the same distinctions between SAFE-NET and other frameworks.

D1.justification: Implementation details, initialization, hyperparameters, sampling and the PyTorch 2.0.0/RTX 3090 setup in Appendix A are unchanged. No technical reproducibility or code/data access information changes.

R1.justification: Research citations, references and positioning in Section 4 and Appendices D–E are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgment introduces no research citation or novelty claim.

P1.justification: v4 adds an 'Acknowledgments and Disclosure of Funding' section after Section 7, inserts a comma after 'To address these shortcomings' on page 2, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining text and organization match.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment heading and paragraph occupy previously blank space on page 17. This is a limited layout addition; all figures, tables, captions, existing content placement and pagination remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 adds a previously absent funding disclosure naming NSF, ONR, Sloan Foundation and IBM Research support, modestly improving transparency and reporting completeness. The punctuation correction is cosmetic, and the scientific evidence, theory and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited.
